content: 1. Administer 1 gram of ertapenem daily via intravenous (IV) or intramuscular (IM) injection for up to 14 days. After at least 3 days of parenteral therapy, if the patient shows clinical improvement, the treatment may be transitioned to an appropriate oral (PO) regimen. 2. For diabetic foot infections, administer 1 gram of ertapenem daily via IV or IM injection for 7 to 14 days. In severe cases, therapy may be extended up to 4 weeks, depending on the severity of the infection and the patient’s response to treatment. Note that this excludes diabetic foot infections with osteomyelitis. 3. In children aged 3 months to 12 years, administer 15 mg/kg of ertapenem via IV or IM injection every 12 hours for up to 14 days, not exceeding 1 gram per dose. After at least 3 days of parenteral therapy, transition to an appropriate oral regimen if the patient improves clinically. 4. In patients older than 12 years, administer 1 gram of ertapenem daily via IV or IM injection for 3 to 14 days, depending on the condition being treated. After at least 3 days of parenteral therapy, transition to an appropriate oral regimen if the patient improves clinically. 5. The safety and efficacy of ertapenem in patients younger than 3 months have not been established. 6. Ertapenem decreases the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. 7. Avoid coadministration of the cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, including ertapenem, as these agents may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 8. Ertapenem may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 9. Ertapenem decreases the levels of valproic acid through an unknown mechanism, potentially increasing the risk of seizures. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Adjust the dose in patients with renal impairment to minimize seizure risk. 10. Ertapenem may reduce the levels or effects of oral contraceptives, such as conjugated estrogens, estradiol, and dienogest/estradiol valerate, by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, additional or alternative forms of birth control may be advisable during concurrent use. 11. Ertapenem may increase the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor patients closely when these agents are coadministered. 12. Ertapenem may decrease the levels or effects of vitamins such as biotin, pantothenic acid, pyridoxine, and thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of these agents. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 13. Probenecid increases the levels of ertapenem by decreasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Ertapenem may decrease the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to activate the drug. Use caution and monitor efficacy when coadministering these agents. 15. Ertapenem is associated with an increased risk of seizures, particularly in patients with a history of seizures or renal impairment. Adjust the dose in moderate to severe renal dysfunction to reduce this risk. 16. Prolonged use of ertapenem increases the risk of superinfections, including Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea. Monitor patients for signs of superinfection during and after treatment. 17. Ertapenem is present in human breast milk. While there are no data on its effects on breastfed infants or milk production, the benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for therapy and potential adverse effects on the infant. 18. Ertapenem should not be co-infused with other medications or diluted with dextrose-containing solutions. 19. Reconstituted IV solutions of ertapenem should be stored at room temperature and used within 6 hours or refrigerated for up to 24 hours and used within 4 hours after removal from refrigeration. Do not freeze. 20. Common side effects of ertapenem include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site, as well as gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and headache. Rarely, it may cause severe intestinal conditions like C. difficile-associated diarrhea, which can occur during or after treatment. 21. Before using ertapenem, inform your healthcare provider if you have allergies to carbapenems, penicillins, cephalosporins, or other medications.
